per_axis.origin_choice: WLS with weights proportional to market share
per_axis.note: Weighting by a regressor (market share) chosen from a residual plot is an unusual but explicitly argued choice (DOC01 p11). It gives large banks most of the weight, which interacts with the outlier deletion of the largest bank's 1987 observation.

overall_design.rationale: A single-market population panel with a within-year demeaned outcome, a summed absolute z-score index and a quadratic term is a conventional 1990s strategy-research design. Three features raise unusualness: (1) WLS with weights equal to deposit market share, so that estimates are dominated by the largest banks; (2) deletion of one named observation of the largest bank, with the deletion reported to have mainly strengthened control variables; (3) a lagged dependent variable in a pooled panel with no fixed effects or clustered inference. None is rare for the period and each is argued in the text, but together they make the focal estimates sensitive to a handful of large-bank observations and to undocumented item mappings for the 11 asset categories.
